files.purpose: The whole per-row vocabulary of the chat transcript: shared timeline geometry constants (TimelineMetrics), the user message bubble with edit/revert, Hydra head report/brief/merge rows and their popovers, the attachment strip and thumbnails, assistant reply rows with their right-click menu, collapsible tool work groups and individual tool rows with diff/image/head popovers, the plan card, todo checklist, notice row, turn-end line, and the collapsed finished-turn block with its file-changes card.

AppKit context menus outlive the right-click, so every menu closure captures value snapshots or weak boxes rather than the SwiftUI row; the file comments say retaining the row pinned its state storage
A documented macOS behavior: a Link nested inside a Button swallows the Button clicks, so the Open link is always a sibling control beside the button, never inside its label

feature_notes: Hover controls are reserved inside the row (22pt) and then subtracted back out of its height with a negative bottom padding, so showing them never moves text and the gap between rows stays exactly 20pt: UserMessageRow uses minus (22 + 6) and AssistantMessageRow minus (22 + 2).

A user message whose text begins with ReplyQuote blocks shows those quotes as separate chips above the bubble so only the typed words stay in the bubble; each chip's help tooltip is the full quoted text and the excerpt is capped at 260pt wide on one line.

The edit pencil only appears when canRevert is true; it toggles runtime.messageEdit (a second tap closes the editor), and merely hovering it calls runtime.revertPreview so the click finds the preview done or nearly so.
Which message is open for editing lives on the thread runtime rather than the row, so leaving a thread only closes the popover and coming back reopens the editor on the same edit.

Right-clicking a user message opens a popover at the pointer with Copy message and Copy as markdown, plus Edit from here when revertable; the menu posts the intent through MessageMenuRequests.confirmRevert and the row then raises the confirmation dialog, so the AppKit menu never retains the row.

HydraReportRow pill summary reads 'Hank is done', 'Hank and Walter are done', 'Hank, Walter and Ada are done'; a head whose '## Name: task (failed)' or '(stopped)' section says otherwise is named with its outcome instead ('Walter failed'), and the whole summary goes through TextCleanup.singleLine with limit 140.
A note from Hydra itself (no heads listed) takes its first line as the pill title with one trailing full stop removed, and everything after that line as the popover body.

If a note body's first line is a bare http:// or https:// URL containing no whitespace, it becomes a sibling 'Open' link and is stripped from the details; if the rest parses as a HydraMergeNote against a MergeRequestLink the popover shows HydraMergePopover, otherwise plain markdown.

HydraHeadsWorkingRow shows only finished heads whose report has not reached the lead: a finished head is included when its batchID still has a running sibling, or, with no batch, when it finished at or after the earliest running head's startedAt; with no running heads at all the list is empty. It reads model.helpers(of: runtime.threadID) rather than scanning model.threads, so writes to other chats do not re-render it.

HydraShimmer sweeps a band across the text every 1.8 seconds at 30 frames per second, band width max(24, width / 3), gradient from Chrome.primaryText opacity 0 to 0.9 at the middle and back to 0; it is entirely absent when NSWorkspace reduce-motion is on and its TimelineView is paused while ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling.

HydraBriefRow decides whether the head is still cooking from whether any other timeline entry shares the brief's turnID, memoized against runtime.entries.count so the scan runs once per count change rather than on every evaluation.

HydraDelegationBlock renders the lead's fenced hydra JSON as a card and never as JSON; it reads partial blocks as they stream through HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations and caches every reading in a 200-entry RecentCache keyed on the raw source string, so a finished block is the same card on every evaluation.
A delegation's project is displayed as just its last path component when the value contains a forward slash.

The merge pill is drawn under the outcome note's own id from the first stage onward, so the single row morphs (contents crossfade while the capsule glides to the new width) instead of being replaced; only the current state's contents take part in layout, drawn as a hidden sizing copy with the live contents overlaid and clipped.
A merging pill for a merge that is over (runtime.isHydraMerging false and no outcome note) removes itself rather than reading 'Merging...' forever.

The merge track's head hops: the arc is zero at every whole dot index and peaks half way between, so a jump over several dots arcs over each one in turn; when the merge is done every dot lights left to right as a wave and the head pops by 18 percent before settling to 18pt while the dots fade.
The merge flourish (track mode .done) fires only when the outcome title contains 'Hydra merged', and lasts 1100 milliseconds before the track falls to .resting.

Both the report pill and the merge pill call MarkdownView.warm off the main thread in a .task as they appear, so a tap finds blocks cached; for a heads' report each head's body is warmed separately from HydraReportDigest.parse(body).heads.

AttachmentThumbnail only mounts its AppKit anchor view after the pointer has hovered it, since a click always follows a hover; an 'anchorless' mode skips the anchor entirely so a strip can keep AppKit views out of SwiftUI's key-view-loop walk and the panel aims at the tap inside the strip's own anchor.
A thumbnail already shown is seeded from ThumbnailMemory in init, so scrolling back to it never fades it in again.

WorkGroup renders a single entry as a bare ToolRow with no header or chevron; a group the agent has moved past (reply text follows it) starts collapsed, and startsCollapsed turning true re-collapses it, but a group the reader opened is never closed on its own (the onChange is one-way).

WorkSteps shows only the last 2 entries and folds the rest behind an 'N earlier steps' line; expanding either a group or the fold calls the revealTimelineEnd action so the view scrolls to keep the end in sight.

ToolPresentation.label strips a leading word that only restates the kind, using per-kind root lists: command [run, bash, shell, exec, execute, command], read [read, view, open, cat], edit [edit, write, multiedit, create, notebookedit, apply_patch, patch], search [search, grep, glob, find], web [fetch, webfetch, websearch, browse], mcp [call], agent [delegate, agent, task], other [use]. So a call titled 'Edit file' reads 'Edited file' rather than 'Edited Edit file'.
MCP calls are recognized by a title of the form '<server> \u00b7 <tool>' (space, middle dot, space) resolved through MCPCatalog.entry(matching:); the label renders as '<entry.name>: <tool>'.

A tool row with non-empty edit paths opens the diff popover; a read with a resolvable image (or any row with an image and no other output) opens the image panel; otherwise a row with output or detail expands inline. A call with none of those renders as a plain line of text rather than a control, so the pointer and VoiceOver treat it as text.

A delegation call whose head thread is not yet linked reads its own title: 'Pip: the merge popover' names the roster persona and the task; otherwise the team's first face stands in and the row says 'a head'. Titles in the set {subagent, agent, task, empty} are treated as the tool's own word for itself and produce no task, so the row never reads 'Delegating Subagent'.

HydraHeadStepsPopover filters the head's entries: the first user message (the brief, shown above) is dropped, later briefs are kept as the lead steering the head on, blank replies are dropped, tool calls and notices are always kept, and reasoning, turnEnd, plan and todos are dropped as the head's own bookkeeping.

Tool output is collapsed to the first 30 lines, counted by scanning the UTF-8 bytes for newline (0x0A) rather than splitting the whole output, because a running command's row re-renders on every flush; the expand button reports the full line count.
Diffs in expanded tool rows are parsed once per distinct (path, diff) pair into a 60-entry RecentCache, so opening and closing a row is instant no matter how large the patch is.

A turn's conclusive answer is defined as the replies that follow its last tool call: reaching for a tool clears the collected answer entries, while plans, notices and checklists do not. A turn that ended on a tool (stopped or failed mid-work) falls back to the last reply it made.
In a collapsed turn, plans and non-info notices stay visible so a failed turn never hides what went wrong; plain info notices only appear when the turn is expanded.
TurnFinishedBlock opens expanded when the chronological timeline setting is on, and folded otherwise; either way the chevron toggles between the answer and the full steps.

TurnFinishedBlock memoizes everything it derives from a turn against a key of the content entries' ObjectIdentifiers plus the expanded flag, and writes the cache in an onChange rather than in the body.

For older turns whose summary carries no changes, the block computes them once through runtime.parsedDiff(selection: turnID) and writes them back with runtime.storeLegacyChanges, guarded on summary.filesChanged > 0 or derived.hasEdits and on Task.isCancelled.

The heads a turn sent out are always listed below the response, folded or not, and are explicitly excluded from the expanded steps (TimelineGroup .heads cases are filtered out) so a head never disappears with the steps.
TurnFileCard's Review button only mounts its NSView anchor after the pointer has hovered it, since a folded turn is a block of a lazy stack and the anchor is only ever needed for a click.
unresolved_questions: HydraMergeRow.mergingContent and mergingLabel are documented as 'the spinner, the stage with its shimmer, the time', but the shipped code draws only the stage Text inside HStack(spacing: 8): the spinner and the elapsed clock were removed and the doc comments left stale. Whether the spinner is expected back cannot be told from this file.
ToolPresentation.mcpLabel(entry:tool:running:) accepts a running flag it never uses, so the label is tense-invariant; whether callers expect a running form is not determinable here.
HydraDelegationBlock's sent flag defaults to false and is set by a caller outside this file, so which timeline code passes sent: true, and at what moment, is unknown from here.

TimelineMetrics.hoverLineHeight (22) is still reserved on both message rows, but the comments say it is kept 'with no copy button left to size it'; whether anything else is meant to occupy that line is not established in this file.
The asset catalog image named badge-edit used by TurnFileCard is not in this file, so its artwork and pixel dimensions are unknown here.

HydraMergeRow indexes the track with runtime.hydraMergeStep?.rawValue against HydraMergeStage.allCases.count; the enum's raw values and their ordering are defined elsewhere and are assumed to be zero-based and contiguous.

FinishedHeadPill composes its visible text from HydraNameStyle.text plus a literal suffix while building a separate title string for the accessibility label; whether the two can diverge for a status outside failed/stopped/completed is not testable from this file alone.
HydraShimmer is applied only to HydraBriefRow's cooking title and to HydraMergeRow's stage words within this file; whether other callers exist is outside this bundle.
